_comment: 2.0-D3 T3 — offline association configuration. Maps an Application Insights component resource id to a .NET app_id (DotNetAppTarget.app_id) and/or a ServiceNow CMDB CI sys_id. Identifiers only: an association names things, it never carries a credential, and an inline credential-looking field is rejected rather than ignored.
_no_inference: Every association here is an explicit operator declaration. Nothing in AgentIQ associates an Application Insights component with a .NET application or a CMDB CI on the basis of a similar name, URL, hostname, IIS site name, resource group, owner, environment, tag, or events happening at similar times. A display name matching in both systems is not evidence.
_shape: Either a JSON object keyed by org id (with a 'default'/'*' fallback) or a plain array applied to every org — the same shape ENTERPRISE_APP_REPOS uses. Live deployments set APP_INSIGHTS_ASSOCIATIONS to the same JSON.
_why_these_entries: The two entries below deliberately name the app_ids the offline .NET fixture (dotnet_app_sample.json) actually configures, so an offline run demonstrates a RESOLVED association rather than reporting a miss. A shipped default that always reported 'declared but not configured' would train operators to ignore the field.
_cmdb_example: A CMDB association is declared the same way, with a CI sys_id, and may be combined with a .NET reference in one entry: {"component_id": "<ARM id>", "dotnet_app_id": "orders-api", "cmdb_ci_sys_id": "a1b2c3d4e5f6000011112222333344455"}. It is not in the default set because a CMDB reference resolves only where MSP-B3 CMDB ingestion has already stored that CI for the org, which an offline run has not done — so including one here would report a permanent miss.

default._case: exact .NET association — the component IS the configured orders-api application
default.notes: Declared by the platform team during onboarding.

default._case: exact .NET association — the component IS the configured inventory-svc application
